Rolling Kendall's tau-b on a tsibble by time window

Source: R/kendall.R
slide_kendall.Rd

slide_kendall() computes Kendall's tau-b between two measured variables over a time-based rolling window. For every observation the window is the half-open time interval (t - .width, t], where t is the value of the index. Only records observed in both variables take part in a window; missings are never imputed, and time points absent from the data never contribute a sample.

Windows overlap, and records enter and leave them in time order. Instead of recomputing the correlation for each window, the concordant and discordant pair counts are carried forward: each record is inserted once and removed once, and tie counts are updated alongside. This yields O(n log^2 n) time and O(n log n) space per key for n records, rather than the quadratic cost of recomputing each window.

Usage

slide_kendall(.x, x, y, .width)

# S3 method for class 'tbl_ts'
slide_kendall(.x, x, y, .width)

# S3 method for class 'grouped_ts'
slide_kendall(.x, x, y, .width)

Arguments

.x

A tsibble with a POSIXct index.

x, y

The two measured variables to correlate, as bare column names or character strings. They must be numeric.

.width

A single positive number giving the window width in seconds. The window contains records with index in (t - .width, t].

Value

A tsibble with the same key, index and grouping as .x, plus the four columns described in Details.

Details

The result keeps the key, index and grouping of .x and appends four columns:

  • n_valid: the number of records in the window observed in both variables.

  • n_concordant: the number of concordant pairs in the window.

  • n_discordant: the number of discordant pairs in the window.

  • tau_b: Kendall's tau-b, (C - D) / sqrt((n0 - n1) * (n0 - n2)), where n0 = n_valid * (n_valid - 1) / 2, and n1 and n2 count the pairs tied in x and in y respectively. It is NA when the denominator is zero, that is when no pair is untied on both sides.

All records sharing an index value receive the same window result; a record whose own variables are missing does not enter any window but still carries the value for its time point. Keys are processed independently, so no state crosses key boundaries.

See also

Other rolling tsibble: slide_tsibble(), stretch_tsibble(), tile_tsibble()

Examples

library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
tick <- tsibble(
  time = as.POSIXct("2020-01-01", tz = "UTC") + c(0, 30, 60, 90, 120),
  price = c(10, 11, 10.5, 12, 12.5),
  volume = c(100, 120, 90, 130, 125),
  index = time
)
tick %>%
  slide_kendall(price, volume, .width = 90)
#> # A tsibble: 5 x 7 [30s] <UTC>
#>   time                price volume n_valid n_concordant n_discordant  tau_b
#>   <dttm>              <dbl>  <dbl>   <int>        <dbl>        <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 2020-01-01 00:00:00  10      100       1            0            0 NA    
#> 2 2020-01-01 00:00:30  11      120       2            1            0  1    
#> 3 2020-01-01 00:01:00  10.5     90       3            2            1  0.333
#> 4 2020-01-01 00:01:30  12      130       3            3            0  1    
#> 5 2020-01-01 00:02:00  12.5    125       3            2            1  0.333

# Per-key, then average the daily correlation
library(lubridate)
tick %>%
  group_by_key() %>%
  slide_kendall(price, volume, .width = 90) %>%
  index_by(Date = ~ as_date(.)) %>%
  summarise(mean_tau_b = mean(tau_b, na.rm = TRUE))
#> # A tsibble: 1 x 2 [?]
#>   Date       mean_tau_b
#>   <date>          <dbl>
#> 1 2020-01-01      0.667
